headline: Wall Street opens where Europe left off: the chip unwind resets the tone, while Hormuz puts a floor under crude

findings.headline: The US open confirms the AI fade, and hike odds go back up
findings.body: Nvidia opened about 5% lower after Monday's 31% surge, with AMD, Micron and Broadcom also falling, while the Dow's value names held up far better than the Nasdaq. The only 14:30 release, the Philadelphia Fed nonmanufacturing survey, rose to 14.3 from 12.9 and gave no reason to price a softer Fed: traders put about 95% odds on a 25bp December hike and 5% on 50bp, as the AI rally itself stoked inflation worries. That leaves Wednesday's GDP and PCE as the next real test of the hike.

findings.headline: Hormuz attacks pull crude off its three-month low
findings.body: UKMTO said three vessels were struck by unidentified projectiles on Monday while sailing east through the Strait of Hormuz, and the WSJ reports the US is investigating whether Iran was behind cyberattacks on as many as 50 tankers. That is fighting a looser supply picture: Deutsche Bank says observed liquids inventories rose in October, implying a 1.7 million b/d surplus, and Libya's Sharara pipeline has reopened. The physical surplus argues for fading spikes, but thin inventory buffers mean a hit to a tanker can still move the front of the curve quickly.

sources.label: CNBC: Oil rebounds from three-month lows on Hormuz threats

findings.headline: Pre-holiday earnings: a strong Best Buy, with Dell the next AI read
findings.body: Best Buy rose after posting its best same-store sales growth in five years, a useful signal for consumer spending going into Black Friday. Dell, HP and Dollar Tree also report before Thanksgiving, and Dell's server orders after the close are the next hard test of whether AI demand justifies Monday's chip rally.

MarketWatch: Dell results on tap, live updates

view: Our view: The US open has reset the tone to risk-off in growth and chips rather than a broad sell-off, since the Dow's value names are holding. With a December hike almost fully priced, the bigger risk into PCE is a hot print that pushes the 50bp tail, not a soft one.
